Path Robotics raises $300 million to expand physical AI for manufacturing

Georgian leads the Series E at a $2.45 billion post-money valuation, supporting welding and adjacent manufacturing tasks.

Path Robotics ↗10 November 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 7

New capital for manufacturing

Path Robotics announced a $300 million Series E led by Georgian at a $2.45 billion post-money valuation, bringing total funding above $610 million. Georgian’s Emily Walsh will join the board. The company intends to use the capital to expand its manufacturing-robotics business.

Welding and adjacent steps

Obsidian combines workpiece perception, joint identification, planning and adjustments during welding. Planned investment includes expanding welding operations and tasks before or after welding, alongside models and computing. Those plans do not establish that every surrounding production step is already automated.

Growth claims and their limits

Path says annual recurring revenue increased 17-fold in 18 months, without disclosing the starting revenue in this announcement. The growth ratio alone cannot establish absolute revenue. This financing is separate from the earlier Rove introduction and HII agreement; agreement values should not be counted as proceeds of this round.
